pins.head: BUY THE POUR, NOT THE KIT
pins.title: Epoxy Resin Kit Size: Work Out the Pour Before You Buy
pins.desc: Kits are sold by total ounces but used by the pour. Measure the mold volume, add a little for the cup and the waste that clings to it, and buy the size that covers the project you actually have. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two bottles of epoxy resin beside graduated measuring cups and an open notepad on a wooden table by a window, with the headline Buy the Pour, Not the Kit.

pins.head: COUNT THE PATCHES
pins.title: Acne Patches: Compare Size, Count and Cost per Patch
pins.desc: A box with more patches is not automatically cheaper if half of them are the wrong size. Count how many of each size a sheet actually gives you, then divide the price by the ones you would really use. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two sheets of hydrocolloid patches in mixed sizes on a white bathroom counter beside a wooden drawer, with the headline Count the Patches.

pins.head: THE DOOR IS A WALL
pins.title: Small Bathroom Storage With No Drilling: Use the Door
pins.desc: The back of the bathroom door is the largest unused surface in the room, and it takes hooks without a single hole. Hang what you reach for daily there and keep the counter for what you use wet. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A small rental bathroom with over-the-door hooks holding towels, a slim rolling cart beside the toilet and a plant on the window ledge, with the headline The Door Is a Wall.

pins.head: THE LEAK YOU HAVEN'T SEEN
pins.title: A Waterproof Under-Sink Mat for the Leak You Have Not Noticed
pins.desc: Under-sink cabinets fail from slow drips, not floods, and particleboard swells long before anyone sees water. A trimmable silicone mat with a raised lip catches it and lifts out for cleaning. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An under-sink kitchen cabinet with visible pipes and a tape measure laid across the base, with the headline The Leak You Haven't Seen.

pins.head: BAGS OR PODS, DO THE MATH
pins.title: Coffee Bags or Pods: Work It Out by the Cup, Not the Pack
pins.desc: A bag and a pod box are priced on different units, so the shelf tells you nothing. Work out cups per week, divide each option by its cup count, and buy the quantity you finish while it is still fresh. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A kraft coffee bag, a stack of coloured coffee pods, a calculator and a notepad on a bright kitchen counter, with the headline Bags or Pods, Do the Math.

pins.head: SIX TUBES IS ENOUGH
pins.title: An Acrylic Starter Palette: Six Tubes Cover Almost Everything
pins.desc: A large set is mostly colours you will never reach for. Two blues, two reds, a yellow and a white mix nearly anything, and learning to mix them teaches more than owning forty tubes ever will. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A craft table with a few acrylic paint tubes and a mixing palette, with the headline Six Tubes Is Enough.

pins.head: WATER IS HEAVY TO SHIP
pins.title: Laundry Detergent Formats: Compare by the Load, Not the Bottle
pins.desc: Liquid is mostly water, and you pay to ship it. Compare formats by cost per load rather than by bottle size, and check the load count on the label rather than the number on the front. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A detergent jug, a box of laundry sheets and a jar of pacs beside folded towels on a laundry shelf, with the headline Water Is Heavy to Ship.

pins.head: MEDIUM TACK DOES IT ALL
pins.title: Medium-Tack Transfer Tape for Everyday Vinyl Decals
pins.desc: High tack lifts the surface underneath and low tack drops the fine cuts. Medium tack is the one roll that handles most decals, and a grid printed on it saves squaring the design by eye. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A cut vinyl decal and a burnishing tool on a green cutting mat at a bright workbench, with the headline Medium Tack Does It All.

pins.head: THE DESK IS NOT STORAGE
pins.title: Small Home Office Organization: Take Storage Off the Desk
pins.desc: Anything stored on the desk becomes the reason the desk is unusable. Move paper to a tray you empty weekly, cables under the surface, and leave the top for the one thing you are working on. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A compact desk with a lamp, a paper tray and a file holder by a window, with the headline The Desk Is Not Storage.
